title: Optimization objectives, constraints and convergence
outcome: Use a prepared optimization library while checking the objective, feasible set and independent convergence evidence.

exercises.title: Check the objective sign
exercises.task: Replace a minimization objective with its negative.
exercises.hint: State whether the goal is minimization or maximization.
exercises.answer: Successful numerical progress cannot validate a mistaken objective definition.

exercises.title: Verify the known optimum
exercises.answer: The test supports this convex fixture rather than a blanket global-convergence claim.

exercises.title: Inspect the feasible set
exercises.task: Minimize the scalar case only on[0,2].
exercises.expected: The best feasible point is near 2.
exercises.answer: Constraints are part of the problem, not an optional display filter.

exercises.title: Read convergence evidence
exercises.task: Inspect the returned point, objective and gradient norm.
exercises.expected: They agree with the known quadratic solution.
exercises.hint: A status flag is only one diagnostic.
exercises.answer: Independent mathematical checks make the optimization result more interpretable.

exercises.title: Scale a parameter
exercises.task: Change a parameter unit in a real objective.
exercises.hint: A numeric rescaling can change the scientific specification.
exercises.answer: Conditioning improvements should retain the original interpretation and feasible decisions.

exercises.title: Assess a fitted model
exercises.task: Observe a lower training objective after optimization.
exercises.expected: Evaluate the frozen procedure on independent data.
exercises.hint: Optimization and generalization are different questions.
exercises.answer: A better fit can still reflect overfitting, leakage or a poor target.
